title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel/disconnect/reconnect and server timeouts
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: streaming RPCs are fragile in the face of client disconnects, cancels and transient network issues which can result in leaked compute, partial responses, and poor developer UX (no reconnection/resume). This PR implements a set of lifecycle controls that (1) allow clients to explicitly cancel streaming requests, (2) detect client disconnects and surface graceful cancellation to the runtime, (3) support reconnect + resume semantics for resumable streams (idempotent resume token), and (4) add server-side idle and hard timeouts to protect capacity. Compatibility: preserves OpenAI-compatible streaming semantics for existing clients; new behavior is opt-in via the stream_lifecycle config flag and resume_token header for older SDKs. Changes include API, runtime, and openai-compat layers, with additional tests and docs. Key behaviors: - Client cancel RPC translates to a SIG-like cancellation delivered to the model worker within 50ms and triggers KV cache rollback where applicable. - On TCP/HTTP disconnect we run a graceful shutdown window (configurable, default 5s) to finish an in-flight token batch before hard cancel. - Reconnect/resume: if client reconnects within resume window (default 30s) with a valid resume_token the server will resume streaming from last acknowledged token; otherwise stream restarts. - Server timeouts: idle timeout (no client ack/ping) defaults to 60s; max stream duration defaults to 5 minutes to prevent runaway usage. Rollout: feature gate enabled for 10% traffic behind flag, with canary metrics in console (stream_reconnect_rate, stream_cancel_latency, leaked_worker_count). Migration notes: SDKs will add resume token helper; OpenAI compat header X-Resume-Token is supported but not required. Tests: unit + integration + e2e simulations of flaky networks, plus a canary against production traffic patterns. See release notes for guidance.
